notes.name: AIM-120, not the original's "AMRAAM": real_weapons.gd keys its own AMRAAM figures on that name
notes.model: the original's file name, which Models: Detailed draws as our AIM-120 (shared/util/gltf.gd STORES: shared/extra/models/stores/aim120.glb); the F-35I carries it inside its bays, shown while their doors are open
notes.generation: 4: the C-7 is in service after 1995 (weapons.ibx's generation 4)
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter (inferred, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (20 kg)
notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one (in the F-35I's bays: none)
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the motion flies the published range from 250 m/s before its flight ends 6 s after the burn (missile.rs real_burn)
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)

footnotes.w-aim120: Wikipedia, "AIM-120 AMRAAM" (AIM-120C-5/6/7: 356 lb, 161.5 kg; 12 ft, 3.65 m; warhead 44 lb, 20 kg; Mach 4; AIM-120C 49 nmi, 90 km) (read 2026-11-10), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIM-120_AMRAAM
footnotes.ds-aim9: designation-systems.net, "Raytheon AIM-9 Sidewinder" (AIM-9A / B effective kill radius about 9 m), https://www.designation-systems.net/dusrm/m-9.html
